# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Customer::bookTrip
Summary: Orchestrates the booking process for a customer on a given trip.
Algorithm:
  Create new Booking instance with given trip, numberOfSeats, current date
  If booking.isBookingEligible() returns true:
    Call booking.updateTripSeats()
    Add booking to this.bookings list
    Add booking to trip.bookings list
    Return true
  Else return false
Related Features: bookings, membershipPackage
Related Classes: Booking, Trip
Input: trip : Trip, numberOfSeats : int
Output: boolean - true if booking was successful, false otherwise
Pre-condition: Customer and trip must be valid objects
Post-condition: If successful, new booking added and trip seats reduced

Customer::computeMonthlyRewardPoints
Summary: Computes reward points earned by a customer during a given month.
Algorithm:
  if membershipPackage is null or !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS) then return 0
  totalPoints = 0
  for each booking in bookings:
    if booking.isInMonth(currentMonth):
      totalPoints += booking.numberOfSeats * 5
  return totalPoints
Related Features: bookings, membershipPackage
Related Classes: Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: currentMonth : String - month in format "yyyy-MM"
Output: int - total reward points earned (0 if ineligible)
Pre-condition: Customer object must exist
Post-condition: No state changes

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Driver::canPostTrip
Summary: Validates whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return false.
Algorithm:
  if newTrip is null then
      return false
  end if
  if newTrip.departureTime is null or newTrip.arrivalTime is null then
      return false
  end if
  // Validate datetime format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm
  if not isValidDateTime(newTrip.departureTime) or not isValidDateTime(newTrip.arrivalTime) then
      return false
  end if
  if newTrip.departureTime >= newTrip.arrivalTime then
      return false
  end if
  for each existingTrip in trips do
      if existingTrip.isTimeConflicting(newTrip.departureTime, newTrip.arrivalTime) then
          return false
      end if
  end for
  return true
Related Features: trips, departureTime, arrivalTime
Related Classes: Trip
Input: newTrip : Trip - the proposed trip to publish
Output: boolean - true if the trip can be published, false otherwise
Pre-condition: The driver exists and has a valid trips list
Post-condition: No state changes

Driver::checkStopOverlap
Summary: Determines whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be false.
Algorithm:
  if trip1 is null or trip2 is null then
      return false
  end if
  stops1 = trip1.getStopStations()
  stops2 = trip2.getStopStations()
  if stops1.isEmpty() or stops2.isEmpty() then
      return false
  end if
  for each station in stops1 do
      if stops2.contains(station) then
          return true
      end if
  end for
  return false
Related Features: stops, getStopStations()
Related Classes: Trip, Stop
Input: trip1 : Trip - first indirect trip; trip2 : Trip - second indirect trip
Output: boolean - true if they share at least one common stop station, false otherwise
Pre-condition: Both trips belong to the same driver
Post-condition: No state changes

    if (!customer.getMembershipPackage().hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS)) {

  public boolean isTimeConflicting(final String newDepartureTime, final String newArrivalTime)

   * Summary: Determines whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's departureTime and arrivalTime as datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return false.
   * Algorithm:
   *   if customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null then
   *       return false
   *   end if
   *   if trip.numberOfSeats - trip.getBookedSeats() < numberOfSeats then
   *       return false
   *   end if

   *       if existingBooking != this and existingBooking.overlapsWith(trip) then
   *           return false
   *       end if
   *   end for
   *   // Check booking time is more than 2 hours before departure
   *   bookingDateTime = parseDateTime(bookingDate.toString() + " " + currentTime) // bookingDate is EDate, need time

   *   // The requirement says "booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours"
   *   // Since bookingDate is EDate (date only), we assume booking time is the current system time on that date
   *   // For simplicity, we compare: departureTime - bookingTime > 2 hours (strictly greater)
   *   if not (departureTime - bookingTime > 2 hours) then
   *       return false
   *   end if
   *   // If all checks pass

public boolean isBookingEligible()
{
    // If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false
    if (getCustomer() == null || getTrip() == null || getBookingDate() == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Check if enough seats available
    if (getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() - getTrip().getBookedSeats() < getNumberOfSeats()) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Check overlapping bookings
    for (Booking existingBooking : getCustomer().getBookings()) {
        if (existingBooking != this && existingBooking.overlapsWith(getTrip())) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    
    // Check booking time is more than 2 hours before departure
    // Parse departureTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
    // bookingDate is a Date, we need to combine with current time or just use the date part
    // The spec says: "booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours"
    // Since bookingDate is EDate (date only), we assume booking time is the current system time on that date
    // For simplicity: departureTime - bookingTime > 2 hours (strictly greater)
    
    try {
        SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
        
        // Get departure datetime
        String departureDateTimeStr = getTrip().getDepartureTime();
        Date departureDateTime = sdf.parse(departureDateTimeStr);
        
        // Booking time: bookingDate + current time
        // Actually, the spec says "bookingDate is EDate, so we need to consider booking time as part of the check"
        // and "booking time is the current system time on that date"
        // So we use the bookingDate at the current time
        Calendar bookingCal = Calendar.getInstance();
        bookingCal.setTime(getBookingDate());
        Calendar now = Calendar.getInstance();
        bookingCal.set(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY, now.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY));
        bookingCal.set(Calendar.MINUTE, now.get(Calendar.MINUTE));
        bookingCal.set(Calendar.SECOND, now.get(Calendar.SECOND));
        Date bookingDateTime = bookingCal.getTime();
        
        // Check if departureTime - bookingTime > 2 hours (strictly greater)
        long diffInMillis = departureDateTime.getTime() - bookingDateTime.getTime();
        long twoHoursInMillis = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
        
        if (diffInMillis <= twoHoursInMillis) {
            return false;
        }
    } catch (ParseException e) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // If all checks pass, book the seats
    getTrip().bookSeats(getNumberOfSeats());
    return true;

public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
{
    if (getTrip() == null || trip == null) {
        return false;
    }
    try {
        SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
        Date thisDeparture = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
        Date thisArrival = sdf.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
        Date otherDeparture = sdf.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
        Date otherArrival = sdf.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
        
        // Check if intervals overlap (allow adjacent boundaries)
        // Two intervals [a, b] and [c, d] overlap if a < d and c < b
        // Adjacent means a == d or c == b, which is NOT overlap
        if (thisDeparture.before(otherArrival) && otherDeparture.before(thisArrival)) {
            return true;
        }
    } catch (ParseException e) {
        return false;
    }
    return false;
}
public boolean isInMonth(final String month)
{
    if (getBookingDate() == null || month == null) {
        return false;
    }
    try {
        SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM");
        String bookingMonth = sdf.format(getBookingDate());
        return bookingMonth.equals(month);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        return false;
    }
}
public void updateTripSeats()
{
    if (getTrip() != null) {
        getTrip().setNumberOfSeats(getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() - getNumberOfSeats());
        getTrip().getBookings().add(this);
    }
}

   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
  {
    if (getTrip() == null || trip == null) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
      Date thisDeparture = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      Date thisArrival = sdf.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
      Date otherDeparture = sdf.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
      Date otherArrival = sdf.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
      // Check if intervals overlap (allow adjacent boundaries)
      // Two intervals [a, b] and [c, d] overlap if a < d and c < b
      // Adjacent (a == d or c == b) is NOT considered overlap
      if (thisDeparture.before(otherArrival) && otherDeparture.before(thisArrival)) {
        return true;
      }
    } catch (ParseException e) {
      return false;
    }
    return false;
  }
